flanker_family: Dior Eau Sauvage (1966) — a DIFFERENT fragrance, not a flanker
bare_mention_means: Dior Sauvage, the 2015 Demachy fresh-spicy — and within that, the EDT by default. The committed entry is CORRECT and the Eau Sauvage risk does not materialise in this corpus: across all 36 comments containing 'sauvage', the string 'eau sauvage' appears ZERO times. Meanwhile 'sauvage edt' appears 6 times and 'sauvage edp' 3, and the corpus was seeded by three 'dior sauvage dupe' videos. Nobody in this corpus is discussing the 1966 citrus.
notes: HIGHEST-RISK ENTRY IN THE SET, AND IT IS FINE — but the risk is real in general, just not here. Eau Sauvage (1966, Roudnitska, lemon/bergamot/basil/oakmoss) and Sauvage (2015, Demachy, bergamot/pepper/ambroxan) are unrelated fragrances that share a house and most of a name. The only thing protecting this corpus is that it was built from 'dior sauvage dupe' searches; a corpus drawn from r/fragrance or from vintage discussion would mix them freely, and 'Sauvage' would need the 'eau' prefix checked before resolving. Recommend adding a negative guard rather than relying on the alias list: 'Eau Sauvage' must never fuzzy-match to 'Sauvage'. At FUZZY_THRESHOLD = 0.88 the two strings are close enough that this is worth testing explicitly. SECOND ISSUE, LIVE NOW: the concentration split inside modern Sauvage is active in this corpus and the current single 'Dior Sauvage' entry will silently swallow it. One commenter writes 'Lattafa Asad is a Dior Sauvage elixir clone ... Neeb is only comparing Dior Sauvage EDT/EDP dupes NOT the Elixir', and another asks for 'a good Dior Sauvage Parfum clone'. Those are claims about Elixir and Parfum, not about Sauvage EDT, and merging them makes the dupe graph wrong in a way no test will catch. Sauvage Elixir in particular has a different note profile (cinnamon, licorice, nutmeg) and its own distinct clone set.

notes: WARNING ABOUT THE CORPUS_MENTIONS METHOD ITSELF, using this row as the example. docs/CURATION.md tells a reviewer to score a flanker by counting its distinguishing word. For Layton that word is 'exclusif' — and 'exclusif' appears 44 times in this corpus. A reviewer applying the documented arithmetic literally would see 44 and conclude the corpus is full of Layton Exclusif talk. It is not: only 6 of those 44 are 'layton exclusif'. The rest belong to OTHER bottles entirely — Delina Exclusif, Pegasus Exclusif, Al Haramain Amber Oud Exclusif, Orientica Xclusif Oud Bleu. The distinguishing word must be counted adjacent to the mention, not free-floating in the corpus. Same failure mode affects 'extrait', 'intense', 'white' and 'elixir'. See VERIFICATION.md.

bare_mention_means: Armaf Club de Nuit Intense Man. The committed entry is CORRECT. The decisive evidence is the abbreviation, not the full name: 'CDNIM' appears 37 times in the corpus as a standalone alias, against 'intense man' 7 times spelled out. Nobody abbreviates a bottle they are not talking about constantly, and the corpus context is uniformly Aventus-clone ('CDNIM is definitely at least as good ... Save the 400 bucks and get the Armaf guys'). The curated alias list already includes CDNIM, which is the right call.
notes: THE WORKED EXAMPLE IN docs/CURATION.md IS FACTUALLY WRONG ABOUT THIS CORPUS, though it reaches the right answer. CURATION.md states, as its central demonstration of the method: "The word that makes it Sillage rather than plain Club de Nuit is 'sillage'. That word appears zero times in your corpus." It appears TEN times. Nine of the ten are the ordinary English perfume noun — 'what about performance and sillage?', 'a sillage/projection monster', 'how much time longevity and sillage and projections'. Exactly one is the product ('This or Club De Nuit Sillage?'). The conclusion in the doc survives (nobody is discussing Club de Nuit Sillage), but the arithmetic it teaches would mislead a reviewer here, and 'sillage' is the single worst possible word to have chosen for the example because it is fragrance vocabulary. Recommend the doc be corrected before more reviewers are trained on it. Also note Armaf's line is far wider than the seed comment's 'and more' suggests, and two of its members already collide with other entries in this file: Club de Nuit Imperiale is the 'Imperiale' mention in Part A, and 'Club de nuit urban man elixir' appears in the corpus as its own bottle.
